title: Trace Rail
prompt: Create a high-fidelity 1440x900 desktop web application UI composition for Curbcut, a browser-native accessibility repair workbench. This must look like a real professional developer tool screenshot, not a poster or marketing page. Precision-light visual world: cool white and pale gray surfaces, near-black ink, disciplined cobalt blue focus, amber proposed state, emerald verified state, restrained red issue severity; no gradients, no neon, no glass, no excessive rounded cards. Composition option A, Trace Rail: a compact horizontal command bar at top with wordmark Curbcut, live WebMCP indicator, Scan, Undo, Import, Export. Below, three synchronized edge-to-edge panes fill almost the full viewport: left source editor with readable HTML line numbers and one exact highlighted source range; center secure checkout live preview with the email input outlined and a small locator badge; right accessibility evidence with serious/critical filters, selected label issue, source location, rationale, and deterministic proposal status. A thin cobalt alignment/trace motif visually links the selected source line, preview target, and issue row without obscuring content. A compact full-width agent action timeline sits at bottom. Show real product text such as label, button-name, tabindex, html-has-lang, Proposal not applied, Human approval required, and 6 affected nodes. Dense but calm, crisp 1px dividers, square-to-6px corners, system UI and tabular mono. No chatbot, no dashboard cards, no illustrations.
